gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-nandinagari: Editorial and unhurried, Quilon swells and thins like brushed watercolor. Noto Sans Nandinagari then keeps its openings generous and its ascenders short, so paragraphs of text move along without snagging.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-newa: Editorial from the first glance, Quilon carries medium-key contrast through every letterform, which gives it its commanding presence. Noto Sans Newa does the quieter job, keeping its lowercase e clearly open.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu holds its terminals far from the stroke body and stands on a towering x-height. Quilon then adds the slight heft change of a stone-carved inscription, so the heading and body pull in different directions.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Quilon leads with stems only a shade heavier than their connecting arms, giving the heading a measured, editorial hand. Noto Sans Ogham keeps wide gaps in the e, so paragraphs read cleanly.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: A gentle ebb and flow of stroke thickness gives Quilon its editorial authority, with moderate shading across round and straight strokes. Noto Sans Old Hungarian keeps its apertures open at the tiniest sizes.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Quilon brings editorial authority through a modest dip in its thin strokes. Noto Sans Old Italic pulls its lowercase up close to cap height, and that tight fit is what sets the pair apart.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ara: Soft pressure, sharp attitude: Quilon shows a faint nib-pressure variation across each round letter. Noto Sans Old North Arabian does the plainer job, with a dense lowercase band and terminals that point outward like tongs.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Noto Sans Old Persian lets its open counters breathe into the white space, lofty and clean. Noto Sans Old Persian and Quilon both hold back, Quilon with mild contrast, never stark.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: A light swell in each bowl, like pressed glass, marks Quilon out as editorial and commanding. Noto Sans Old Turkic brings chunky lowercase and open-mouthed curves, which is the pair's clearest contrast.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Editorial and restful, Quilon keeps its line to modest swings in stroke weight. Noto Sans Oriya stands out for small letters nearly as high as the capitals, with generous gaps in its curves.
